subject: POC Trial: Success Criteria & KPIs - Atlas Payments
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Reynolds <alex.reynolds@atlas-payments.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 14 Jun 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: POC Trial: Success Criteria & KPIs - Atlas Payments

Alex / Sofia — thanks again for the time today. Quick post-call recap and proposed next steps for the POC/trial so we have alignment before kickoff. Attaching a lightweight KPI template (atlas-poc-kpi-template.xlsx) and our runbook (redwood-poc-runbook.pdf).

Summary of what we heard:
- Objective: validate Redwood inference as the production runtime for chat + transaction classification for Atlas Payments (customer support triage + post-transaction risk signals).
- Scope: evaluate model serving performance on a representative workload (live-ish traces + synthetic transactions), confirm quality on labeled eval set, and measure unit economics (cost/token).

Proposed success criteria (please review / tweak):
1) Latency: 95th percentile end-to-end latency < 200 ms for customer-facing chat flows (95p including network + model).
2) Throughput: sustain 150 requests/sec p95 (steady-state with burst handling up to 300 req/s for short periods).
3) Cost: average cost/token <= $0.0005 (measured across evaluation workload).
4) Quality: human-rated correctness >= 90% on critical intents (fraud flagging / risk signal) and automated precision >= 92% on labeled set.
5) Reliability: zero critical errors during 48h soak; error rate < 0.5% for 5xx or timeouts.

Evaluation plan / owners / timeline (proposed):
- Week 0 (6/20) Kickoff + infra setup (owner: Jordan + Stephanie).
- Week 1 (6/21-6/27) Run curated evals: 10k labeled queries from Atlas (owner: Marissa).
- Week 2 (6/28-7/4) Soak test + burst/throughput testing with production traces (owner: Stephanie).
- Deliverable: final KPI report + recommendations and configuration to meet targets (owner: Jordan).

Next steps:
- Please confirm owners and targets (especially latency and quality thresholds) by EOD 6/16.
- If confirmed, we’ll schedule a 30-min kickoff on 6/20 (proposed 10am PT).

Attachments: atlas-poc-kpi-template.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood-poc-runbook.pdf (setup + test checklist).

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Jordan — thanks for the clear recap. This looks great and aligns with what we discussed. A couple of quick notes / requests from our side:

- Latency: the 200ms 95p is acceptable as a target. For chat flows that influence conversion we’d like to see a 50ms median target if possible, but we won’t block on that for the POC.
- Quality: can you add an automated sampling plan for human review? We want a daily 200-sample blind review during the soak window.
- Cost: Atlas is cost-sensitive; the $0.0005/token looks right as a goal — please include the tokenization assumptions in the KPI sheet.

We confirm owners on our side: Sofia will coordinate labelled data and access to traces (Sofia copied). We can meet 6/20 10am PT.

One ask: can your SE produce a quick note on how you measure p95 latency (client-side vs model-only vs end-to-end)? That will help us compare against our internal telemetry.

— Alex
Alex Reynolds

Atlas Payments

Hi all — quick technical note on measurement and environment so expectations are aligned:

- End-to-end p95: we’ll instrument a lightweight client harness (running from Atlas test network or a Redwood-proxied tester in same region) to capture network + request/response time. That gives you the user-observed p95.
- Server/model p95: Redwood will report model compute p95 and queue latency p95 from the GPU host.
- Throughput testing: we’ll run fixed QPS sweeps and a production-trace replay (you provide traces). For the throughput target (150 req/s sustained) we’ll run a 1-hour steady-state window and a separate 10-minute burst at 300 req/s to validate graceful degradation.
- Token accounting: we’ll capture token counts per request using the tokenizer used for the model, and include tokenization assumptions in the KPI spreadsheet.
- Data handling: Atlas-provided traces will be isolated and purged after the trial; we can run in Dedicated mode for isolation if you prefer (extra provisioning lead time).

I’ve attached the Redwood POC runbook (redwood-poc-runbook.pdf) with the instrumentation checklist. No blockers from SE side — we’re good to start 6/20.

— Stephanie
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
